newsitem.title: COMOROS: Hijacked Ethiopia plane crashes in sea near Comoros.
newsitem.headline: Hijacked Ethiopia plane crashes in sea near Comoros.

text.p: A hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 with about 178 passengers and crew aboard crashed into the sea near the Comoro Islands on Saturday.
A witness said about 100 bodies had been recovered and there were some 30 survivors.

Frederick Chretien, manager of a beach hotel near where where the airliner landed, told the BBC World Service that the plane apparently came down because it ran out of fuel and there was no explosion before the crash.
"We've got survivors. They are in hospital close to the hotel. At the last information there are about 30 survivors," he added, saying that about 100 bodies had been recovered.
Chretien said a survivor had spoken of seeing two hijackers on board.
A senior official with the airline, Guenet Berhe, told Reuters earlier that the identity and motives of the hijackers were unknown.
The plane was hijacked on Saturday morning soon after it took off from Addis Ababa to Abidjan via Nairobi, Brazzaville and Lagos.
Witnesses earlier said the plane broke in two when it plunged into the sea only metres (yards) from shore next to the Galawa beach hotel about 40 km (25 miles) north of Moroni.
"The plane crashed at around 3:20 local time (1220 GMT)," Chakira Maamoune, a senior Moroni airport official, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"I can confirm that the airplane was not in contact with Moroni air traffic control," he said.
Ethiopian Airlines officials in the Tanzanian capital Dar es Salaam said they made contact with the plane at about 3 p.m. (1200 GMT).
"The control tower had some contact with the plane but only for five minutes, then it was cut. At that point the plane was around the coastal area of Dar es Salaam," the official said.
Mauritian state television reported that the hijackers had wanted to go to Mauritius and the airport there was put on full alert. It did not say whether the plane was refused permission to land.
The plane was hijacked soon after it left Addis Ababa on scheduled flight ET 961 to Abidjan.
After the hijackers took control, it entered Tanzanian airspace and flew east across the Indian Ocean heading for the Comoro Islands.
Earlier the state airline's general manager, Ahmed Kellow, told Reuters: "We have very little knowledge of who the hijackers are or their demands."
Ethiopian Airlines is the only airline that crosses the breadth of Africa and has had one of the best safety records among African carriers.
